title: Allow more than 3 decimals for valid time string, matching parser definition
body:
A [valid time string](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-time-string) can only have 3 numbers after the decimal separator in seconds, as defined in 4.3.2.:

> One, two, or three ASCII digits, representing the fractional part of second

However, when [parsing a time component](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#parse-a-time-component) any number of digits (an uncapped “sequence of code points”) is accepted according to step 7.3.:

> Collect a sequence of code points that are either ASCII digits or U+002E FULL STOP characters from input given position. If the collected sequence is three characters long, or if it is longer than three characters long and the third character is not a U+002E FULL STOP character, or if it has more than one U+002E FULL STOP character, then fail. Otherwise, interpret the resulting sequence as a base-ten number (possibly with a fractional part). Set second to that number.

So `second` may be set to something like `12.3456789`, but if this were to be written out it no longer matches the definition of a valid time string as quoted above.

I propose dropping the limitation on digits representing the fractional part unless there is a good reason to force such a thing on users. The parsing already supports it.
